---
title: The template file
description: Every block a template may contain, and the defaults for the ones it leaves out
---

A template is one YAML file, `template.yaml` at the root of its
repository — see [Publishing](/docs/templates/publishing). This is the
worked example the validator's own tests run against — [Umami](https://umami.is), one app and one
database:

```yaml
version: 1
minCubeship: "0.6.0"
project: umami            # suggested slug; the installer may change it

inputs:                   # what the template cannot know
  - key: domain
    type: domain
    label: Where the dashboard answers
  - key: appSecret
    type: secret
    label: The app's session secret
    generate: 32          # the instance generates it and shows it once

databases:
  - key: db                # template-local; what references name
    name: umami-db         # suggested instance name, renamable at install
    engine: postgres
    version: "18"
    database: umami        # the password is generated, never written here

apps:
  - key: web
    name: web
    image: ghcr.io/umami-software/umami
    tag: postgresql-v2
    port: 3000
    health: /api/heartbeat
    domains:
      - host: ${input.domain}
    attach:
      - database: db      # contributes DATABASE_URL and friends
        prefix: ""
    limits: { cpu: 1, memory: 1Gi }
    scale: 1
    env:
      APP_SECRET: ${input.appSecret}
      DATABASE_TYPE: postgresql
```

Every key not shown below is optional and takes the default listed.
Unknown keys are refused — see [`schema.unknown-key`](/docs/templates/diagnostics#schemaunknown-key).

## Top level

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | — | Always `1`. The only value the validator speaks right now. |
| `minCubeship` | none | A [semver range](https://github.com/npm/node-semver#ranges) the installing instance must satisfy, e.g. `">=0.6.0"`. |
| `project` | — | The suggested project slug. The installer may rename it. |
| `environment` | `production` | The suggested environment inside that project. |
| `inputs` | `[]` | What the installer is asked. See [Inputs](/docs/templates/inputs). |
| `databases` | `[]` | The managed databases this template needs. |
| `stores` | `[]` | The managed object stores this template needs. |
| `apps` | — | At least one. What actually runs. |

## Keys and names are two different things

Every input, database, store and app has a `key` — lowercase or mixed
case, letters/digits/dash/underscore, starting with a letter — which
never leaves the file. It is what a reference like `${db.db.host}`
names, and what `attach.database` or `attach.store` names, and it is
how one part of the template points at another. See
[References](/docs/templates/references).

A database, store or app also has a `name`, which defaults to its
`key` and is what appears on the instance. The installer may change any
name, and for databases and stores it sometimes has to: their names are
unique across the whole instance, so two installs of one template would
collide on the first one otherwise.

## Databases

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | — | Required. What `attach` and `${db.<key>.…}` name. |
| `name` | the key | The suggested instance name. |
| `engine` | — | Required. One of `postgres`, `mysql`, `mariadb`, `redis`, `mongodb`. |
| `version` | the newest offered | Pinning it is [advised](/docs/templates/diagnostics#adviceunpinned-engine) but not required. |
| `extensions` | none | Postgres only. A list of [extension names](#extensions) the database is created with. |
| `username` | the engine's default | Redis is always `default`; MySQL and MariaDB refuse `root`. |
| `database` | none | The database name inside the engine. Ignored on engines with none, like Redis. |
| `expose` | not exposed | `null` (the default) keeps it internal only; `0` asks for a port picked for you; a number asks for that port. |
| `limits` | none | See [Limits](#limits-and-scaling). |

There is no `password` field. A database's password is generated by
the instance and handed to an app through
[an attachment](#attach) — a template that could write one down
would be a template that could steal one.

### Extensions

A Postgres database can be created with extensions:

```yaml
databases:
  - key: db
    engine: postgres
    version: "16"
    extensions:
      - pgvector
      - vectorchord
```

Names, not packages. Cubeship accepts only the ones it has reviewed, and
each one picks a fixed statement — and, for two of them, a specific
image pinned by digest. Nothing in a template reaches a Dockerfile, a
package manager or a SQL string.

The name you write is Cubeship's, and it is not always the name the
extension has in SQL: `pgvector` creates the extension `vector`, and
`vectorchord` creates `vchord`. Your migrations use the SQL name.

The list is **normalized**: duplicates go, it is sorted, and what an
extension requires is added — `vectorchord` brings `pgvector`,
`earthdistance` brings `cube`. So `[vectorchord]` and
`[pgvector, vectorchord]` are the same template.

Most of them are PostgreSQL's own contrib modules, which every image
Cubeship runs already carries: `pg_trgm`, `pgcrypto`, `hstore`,
`citext`, `ltree`, `unaccent`, `uuid-ossp`, `btree_gin`, `btree_gist`,
`bloom`, `cube`, `earthdistance`, `fuzzystrmatch`, `intarray`, `isn`,
`seg`, `tablefunc`, `tsm_system_rows`, `dblink`, `postgres_fdw`,
`pg_prewarm`, `pgstattuple`, `pg_buffercache` and `pg_stat_statements`.
Two are not — `pgvector` and `vectorchord` — and those run an image of
their own. `GET /datastores/engines` on an instance is the list it will
actually accept, per version.

A template with extensions needs a `minCubeship` that excludes releases
before them. An older instance installs the template happily and creates
the database **without** them, which is an app that comes up and fails on
its first query.

A later release of a template that changes a database's extensions does
not change a database that already exists — the preview says so, the
same way it does for an engine or a version. Extensions can be installed
on the database itself afterwards, from its own page.

## Stores

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | — | Required. What `attach` names. |
| `name` | the key | The suggested instance name. |
| `version` | none | The MinIO version, unvalidated here — the instance decides what a missing one means. |
| `buckets` | `[]` | The buckets to create inside it. |
| `limits` | none | See [Limits](#limits-and-scaling). |

A template cannot declare a linked S3 endpoint — that would be
somebody's credential. A template that wants one asks for an
[input of type `store`](/docs/templates/inputs) instead, and the
installer picks a store that already exists on the instance.

## Apps

### Source

An app is exactly one of an image or a build — never neither, never
both:

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `image` | none | A public image, with no tag in the string — `tag` is its own field. |
| `tag` | none | The tag for `image`. Refused on a build: a built app is tagged by its deploy, not by you. |
| `repo` | none | An `http`, `https` or `git` URL, with the branch in `ref`, never after a `#`. |
| `ref` | the repo's default branch | The branch or tag to build. |
| `build` | none | `dockerfile` or `railpack`. Required once `repo` is set. |
| `dockerfile` | `Dockerfile` | Only meaningful with `build: dockerfile`. |

### Network

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `port` | none | The port the app listens on. Also the default for a domain that names none. |
| `health` | off | A path starting with `/`, no `?` or `#`, at most 255 characters. Strongly advised — see [`advice.no-health`](/docs/templates/diagnostics#adviceno-health). |
| `domains` | `[]` | See below. |

Each entry under `domains` is `{ host, port }`. `host` must come from
exactly one [input of type `domain`](/docs/templates/inputs) —
`${input.<key>}` and nothing else, never a literal hostname. `port`
defaults to the app's own `port`, and beneath that to `8080`.

### Attach

Each entry under `attach` wires one database or one store into the
app's environment — exactly one of `database` or `store` per entry,
naming its `key`:

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | — | A database's key, exclusive with `store`. |
| `store` | — | A store's key, or the key of an [input of type `store`](/docs/templates/inputs), exclusive with `database`. |
| `bucket` | — | Required with `store`: which bucket the app gets. |
| `prefix` | `""` | Upper case, ending in `_`, like `ANALYTICS_`. Distinguishes two attachments that would otherwise write the same variable names. |

A database attachment contributes `<PREFIX><STEM>_URL`, `_HOST`,
`_PORT`, `_USER`, `_PASSWORD`, and `_NAME` unless the engine has no
named databases — `STEM` is `DATABASE` for postgres, mysql and
mariadb, `REDIS` for redis, `MONGO` for mongodb. A store attachment
contributes `<PREFIX>S3_ENDPOINT`, `_REGION`, `_BUCKET`,
`_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `_PATH_STYLE`.

### Environment

`env` is a map of names to values, merged into the app on top of
whatever `attach` already wrote — an app's own `env` wins on a
collision, which is how you point at a different target without
detaching anything. A value may itself be a
[reference](/docs/templates/references), like `${input.appSecret}`
above.

### Limits and scaling

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `limits.cpu` | none | Cores, at least `0.01`. |
| `limits.memory` | none | A size — `512Mi`, `2Gi`, `1500M` — at least `6Mi`. |
| `scale` | none | How many copies, at least `1`. |
| `spread` | `false` | Spread copies across machines rather than pack them onto one. |
| `autoscale.min` | `1` | The floor, at least `1` and at most `max`. |
| `autoscale.max` | — | Required with `autoscale`. At most `100`. |
| `autoscale.cpu` | — | Required with `autoscale`. A target above `0`, where `100` means one whole core. |

`limits` and `stores`/`databases`' own `limits` share the same shape.

### Volumes

```yaml
apps:
  - key: broker
    image: rabbitmq
    volumes:
      - path: /var/lib/rabbitmq
```

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `volumes[].path` | — | An absolute path inside the container whose contents survive deploys and restarts. Not `/`, not under `/proc`, `/sys` or `/dev`. |

A volume is for software that keeps its state in files — a queue, a
search index. **An app with a volume runs as one copy on one machine**,
so `scale`, `spread` and `autoscale` are refused beside it, and each
deploy stops the old container before starting the new one: the app is
briefly unavailable. A template with a volume needs `minCubeship: "0.7.0"`
or later, so an older instance refuses it instead of installing it
without its data surviving. Uninstalling keeps volume data unless
whoever uninstalls says otherwise.

### TCP ports

```yaml
inputs:
  - key: sshPort
    type: number
    label: The port SSH answers on
    default: 2222
    min: 1024
    max: 65535
apps:
  - key: git
    image: gitea/gitea
    tcp:
      - port: 22
        host: ${input.sshPort}
```

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tcp[].port` | — | The port the app listens on inside its container, `1`-`65535`. |
| `tcp[].host` | picked | Where the instance publishes it: `1024`-`65535`, or `${input.<key>}` naming a `number` input. Left out, the instance picks a free one from `17000`-`17999`. |

A TCP port is for a protocol that is not HTTP — SSH into a Git server, a
game server, a broker. It is published on the instance's own address with
**no TLS and no proxy** in front of it, so the app's own authentication is
what protects it. **An app with a TCP port runs as one copy**, so `scale`,
`spread` and `autoscale` are refused beside it, and each deploy stops the old
container before starting the new one.

Name the host port through an input rather than as a number: a port another
installation already holds is refused, and the person installing is the one
who knows which is free. A template with a TCP port needs
`minCubeship: "0.7.2"` or later.
